The agentic platform that learns your compliance program and runs it end-to-end. Investigations are fully auditable, connected to trusted data sources, and committed to an organizational memory that compounds.

Every case makes your entire system smarter. A precedent set by one investigator is instantly available across KYC, EDD, sanctions, and monitoring. Whether your team is five analysts or 500, they share one brain – with the full risk picture assembled for the first time. Every memory has provenance. Agents propose; humans approve.

With pre-built integrations across LexisNexis, Experian, ComplyAdvantage, government registries and beyond, Percy is directly connected to the source of truth. Whenever a finding is escalated, it comes alongside context – grounded in the data you already trust.

Percy touches 100% of your alert and case volume, reviewing with greater speed and precision. Percy pulls data, cross-references sources, and documents its reasoning around the clock – so your team can apply their judgement with more context and efficiency.
Your policies and procedures, automated

Percy doesn’t impose a workflow, it learns yours. When you feed it your existing procedures, it executes them deterministically. That means you get the same outcome every time, with a full audit trail. This is the continuity that unlocks cross-functional teams – empowering them with consistent policies and information, while saving them from duplicating work.
Risk leaders need to know about problems before they happen, not after.
Percy is our agentic system that investigates every case, surfaces every relevant finding, and runs your policies and procedures end-to-end.

Percy works in plain English. You can ask it to investigate a case, explain its reasoning, surface similar patterns, or create a new workflow — no coding or configuring necessary. Percy will provide an answer — grounded in data — in seconds.
Every change is versioned and tested before it goes live — so Percy gets better at your program over time, instead of drifting away from it.

Customers rely on us for decisions that affect their business and their risk. We need to understand what they’re trying to do and where we’re making it harder. That means getting on calls, asking questions, and helping resolve problems wherever they start.

We take on problems we don’t yet know how to solve. When we get stuck, we’re honest about what’s hard and work out what to try next. Nobody is expected to have every answer, but everyone is expected to help find one.
